$why: MIT obliges the fork to carry upstream's copyright and to name what it forked. The earlier
design discharged that by freezing upstream strings in place. That is wrong here: every
obra/superpowers occurrence in upstream's README is an install instruction for upstream's own
distribution channels, so freezing them ships a README that installs the wrong plugin.
So attribution is ASSERTED on the built tree instead of frozen in the source: we author the
text, and the build refuses if the credit is missing. An assertion cannot rot into a stale
protected string the way a freeze can.

require.reason: MIT: the upstream copyright notice must survive redistribution byte-for-byte
MIT attribution: the fork must name upstream, its author and its repository, and state that it is a fork
attribution in the manifest description, which is what a user sees in /plugin without opening the README

thresholds.$comment: A3: changedFilesPct is a starting value, not a measurement - calibrate over the first real updates. A threshold that never fires is decoration; one that always fires is noise. The other two are absolutes: a build that cannot classify an upstream file, or that has lost its attribution, must never be published.
